newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums firm on French strike.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums firm on French strike.

text.p: An oil workers' strike affecting a quarter of French refining capacity helped lift NWE gas oil cargo premiums slightly in thin trade on Tuesday but NYMEX strength kept a lid on barge demand, traders said.
Dec IPE futures finished $3 higher at $222.75 a tonne, lifted by NYMEX heating oil which rose from early lows.
A refinery grade heating oil cargo traded around $1 firmer at Dec IPE +$7.75 for December 1-10 delivery cif Germany, with a similar cargo later bid at +$8.50.
Heating oil for delivery December 10-10 was offered at +$9.50 into Germany and Le Havre.
A low sulphur diesel cargo was traded at Dec IPE +$21 cif Lorient.

Bulls said the French stoppage could result in a shortfall of hundreds of thousands of tonnes of gas oil in NWE even if it ended this week. Bears said the resulting supply gap might only be only a fraction of that, and noted weather was relatively mild. Cargo traders were exploring an arbitrage to the U.S.

On barges, firmness in New York heating oil dampened ARA demand and volumes. Low sulphur diesel was offered at Dec IPE +$13. A heating oil refinery grade barge traded at Dec IPE +$2 early in the day but product was later offered at +$1.50.
